title: Handshakes at the Party
summary: Solve smaller versions first and look for the pattern.

steps.title: The puzzle
sentences: Five friends meet. Each shakes hands with every other friend exactly once.
points: Five friends meet. Each shakes hands with every other friend exactly once.

steps.title: How to think about it
sentences: Counting one by one is easy to mess up.
Look for a pattern with smaller groups first.
points: Counting one by one is easy to mess up.

steps.title: The method: Try smaller cases
sentences: With 2 friends: 1 handshake. With 3 friends: 3. With 4 friends: 6.
Each new friend adds a handshake with everyone already there.
points: With 2 friends: 1 handshake. With 3 friends: 3. With 4 friends: 6.

steps.title: The answer
sentences: For 5 friends we add 4 more to the 6, which gives 10.
There is also a shortcut: each person shakes 4 hands, so 5 times 4 is 20, and each handshake was counted twice, so divide by 2 to get 10.
points: For 5 friends we add 4 more to the 6, which gives 10.

facts: For n people the handshakes are n times (n minus 1) divided by 2.
